what: Lattice Semiconductor makes small, low-power programmable logic chips. They sit in servers, communications equipment, industrial systems and cars, handling control and interface tasks that fixed-function chips cannot be reprogrammed to do.
customers: Server and data centre equipment makers, communications infrastructure companies, industrial automation and automotive suppliers.
money: small field-programmable gate arrays and related silicon
design software and licensed intellectual property
moat: The lowest-power small programmable chips available, designed into systems where power and board space are tight and alternatives are far larger.
risks: Revenue has fallen about 7% a year over three years after a severe inventory correction
Debt of about $925 million against very little cash
The shares trade at a very high multiple of current earnings
opportunities: Gross margin of 68%, high for a chipmaker, means a recovery converts quickly to profit
Analysts see about 36% upside from current levels
AI server designs use its chips for power management and security control
watch: Revenue recovery against the inventory correction, and design wins in servers.
